name: The Redwood of the Pincio
evidence: Aerial imagery check per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's standing tool. Esri World Imagery (Vantor/Maxar WV03, Vivid Advanced, 0.31m resolution, capture date 2025-11-05, verified via the MapServer /identify endpoint before use) shows a single tree with a narrow, dark, distinctly conical crown standing at the edge of a small fountain clearing on the Pincio terrace, exactly at the Lazio register's GIS-surveyed coordinate (41.911639, 12.479611, converted independently from the register's own DMS 41°54'41.9"N 12°28'46.6"E and matching to 6 decimal places). It casts a long, narrow, single shadow markedly different in shape from the flatter, umbrella-shaped shadows of the stone pines (Pinus pinea) that dominate the rest of the terrace canopy in the same image, consistent with a tall, narrow-crowned conifer distinct from its neighbours and individually identifiable, i.e. the aerial-evidence bar for 'position, when the tree is individually identifiable: a distinctive crown'. This is new evidence beyond what the 2026-08-08 pass had (which found no Commons photo and no independent corroboration and, applying the Caserta lesson, kept the pin approximate on that basis alone). The register coordinate is not address-level: the source columns are explicitly labelled 'LATITUDINE su GIS' / 'LONGITUDINE su GIS', i.e. a GIS-surveyed point, and it now has independent visual corroboration.
verify_notes: Recommend flipping rom_016's location_precision from 'approximate' to 'confirmed'. Everything else about the entry (single-source narrative uncertainty, 'among the five tallest' superlative, age undocumented) is unchanged and still correctly flagged; this update is about the PIN only, not the story's confidence. Images saved for reference during this pass are not part of the delivery (no photo ships without its own open licence per hard rule 4); this was a position check only, never a photo source.

name: The Cypress of Piazza di Siena
evidence: Same Esri World Imagery pass (2025-11-05, 0.31m) clearly shows the row of cypresses lining the near (northwest) side of the Piazza di Siena oval, individually resolvable with distinct shadows. But the shadows are visually uniform in length across the row: no single tree stands out as obviously older or larger than its neighbours the way rom_016's redwood stands out from the surrounding pines. Since no source names which specific cypress along the perimeter is the 1789 survivor, and aerial imagery cannot itself distinguish a 235-year-old cypress from a well-grown ornamental replacement without a visible size anomaly, this does not clear the confirmed bar. Left approximate, honestly, per the brief: 'if a pin cannot be confirmed, leave it approximate and say so.'

name: The Hackberries of the Aranciera
evidence: RAMI (ilregistrodeglialberi.it) register pages for both folded ids (#9251, #9252) checked directly: both explicitly state 'Coordinate: Non disponibile' (coordinates not available), only the locality 'Villa Borghese (Museo B)', which matches what we already had, not an improvement. Aerial imagery (2025-11-05, 0.31m) of the Lecceta shows dense, uniform holm-oak-dominated canopy around the Aranciera/Museo Carlo Bilotti building with no individually resolvable trees or texture differences visible from directly overhead; a hackberry pair inside a closed-canopy wood cannot be picked out from satellite imagery alone. Stays approximate.

name: Pino dell'Himalaya (Chir Pine), Villa Fiorelli
note: The only genuinely unresearched register candidate within reach this pass (all other 'no flag' entries in the passcheck brief's 38-candidate list turned out, on cross-check against data/registers/italy-masaf.json sheet ids, to already be accounted for: sheets 28/29/30/73 are the blocked San Sisto nursery, sheets 13/14 are the already-published Celimontana cedar/pine, sheet 65 and sheet 75 are existing unresolved leads, and everything past 6km is outside the day-trip-relevant spread). WebSearch repeatedly surfaced a claim that this pine is a 'twin' of the published Colle Oppio Chir Pine (rom_020), both by Raffaele De Vico; this could NOT be corroborated by direct WebFetch of the sources the search cited (Wikipedia IT, sovraintendenzaroma.it's own Villa Fiorelli page, an innamoratidiroma.it Colle Oppio piece): none of the three, read directly, contain any mention of a pine, a 'twin', or Raffaele De Vico plus a specific tree. Treating the search engine's synthesis as unverified rather than as a second source, per 'never fabricate'. Sheet 70 remains a register-only lead, ~2.4km from the Celimontana cluster (outside the ~2km walk radius), access and vitality both still unconfirmed. Updated data/leads/rome.json with this negative search result so a future pass does not repeat it.
